note: Unlisted server and rack makers (scope agreed with the owner: whole servers and rack integration only; cooling and power start-ups are listed by name, not researched). Compiled 2026-11-09 from IPO documents, regulatory filings, company releases and media, then adversarially re-checked against the cited pages the same day (23 claims: 18 confirmed, 4 partly, 1 wrong and corrected here: Oxide's October 2026 Series D was missing). Funding facts need two independent sources; a round with one source says so. curator_notes stay in this file and never reach data/facts.

rows.name: xFusion
rows.origin: Huawei's x86 server business, carved out in 2021; Huawei has fully exited
rows.status: IPO under review (Shenzhen ChiNext; application accepted 2026-05-22, listing committee 2026-11-12)
rows.builds: x86 and AI servers, liquid-cooled racks; since 2024 more domestic-chip (Ascend/Kunpeng) servers than x86
rows.funding: Huawei sale price cut from RMB 57.0bn (2021) to 33.0bn (2025); a December 2025 round at RMB 43.0bn pre-money (one source)
rows.why: The largest private server maker by revenue, and its prospectus shows the same margin squeeze as the listed pool: gross margin down six points in two years as AI mix rose.
rows.caveat: Prospectus-draft figures as reported by 上海证券报, not the final listing document; the listing committee had not met when this was recorded.
rows.curator_notes: Committee date from eastmoney 2026-11-06 body (wap.eastmoney.com/a/202611053923810646.html). Price cut and Dec-2025 round from finance.ifeng.com/c/8xnXUPjh4U0 (author 宋旭光/市研), single source for the round.

rows.name: Nettrix
rows.status: Private; on the US Entity List since 2025-03-25; no IPO filing found
rows.builds: AI and general-purpose servers; ranked second in China accelerated servers by sales in IDC's 2022H1 tracker
rows.revenue: Not published (an encyclopedia figure circulates; not used)
rows.why: Shows US export controls reaching private Chinese whole-machine makers, not only the listed ones.
rows.caveat: No audited financials have ever been published; its scale is known only from vendor rankings.
rows.curator_notes: Not linked to Inspur despite aggregator claims. Baidu Baike 2023 revenue 210.21亿 is single-source; excluded.

rows.name: ZT Systems
rows.status: Acquired by AMD (closed 2025-03-31); manufacturing sold to Sanmina (closed 2025-10-27, up to US$3.0bn)
rows.builds: Rack-scale systems for the largest cloud companies; AMD kept the rack design team
rows.revenue: Manufacturing run-rate about US$5-6bn a year (Sanmina, at signing)
rows.funding: AMD's announced value in August 2024: US$4.9bn including up to US$400m contingent
rows.why: A chip company paid for rack design and then sold the factories: the design layer was worth keeping, the assembly layer went to a contract manufacturer.
rows.caveat: The run-rate is the buyer's statement at signing, not a reported fiscal-year figure.
rows.curator_notes: US$4.9bn from AMD 2024-08-19 announcement and media; not in the closing 8-K. Sanmina terms from ir.sanmina.com 2025-05-19.

rows.name: Huakun Zhenyu
rows.origin: Chengdu state-controlled maker in the Huawei Kunpeng/Ascend ecosystem
rows.status: Private; a listed sister company's purchase of 70% was terminated in 2024
rows.builds: Ascend AI servers and Kunpeng servers; largest share (6,144 of 20,480 cards) in China Mobile's 2026-27 AI super-node shortlist
rows.why: The domestic-chip tier is large and thin: RMB 12.6bn of revenue on about RMB 0.46bn of net assets in 2024.
rows.caveat: Figures from capital-increase documents on an equity exchange as quoted by media, not an audited public filing.
rows.curator_notes: Tender: the '>117亿' figure is the whole project's bid price, not Huakun's award. 2025 revenue 148.4亿 only from a Xueqiu post; excluded.

rows.name: PowerLeader Computing
rows.origin: Shenzhen maker in the Huawei ecosystem since 1997
rows.status: Being acquired by listed 慧博云通 (65.47% for RMB 2.946bn in shares; still pending at 2026-09)
rows.builds: Kunpeng, Ascend, Hygon and Phytium servers; second in China Mobile's 2026-27 AI super-node shortlist
rows.revenue: Not published in the sources read; sellers promise net profit of at least RMB 190m for 2025
rows.why: A reference price for a second-tier domestic-chip server maker, reached by a reverse sale after its own IPO preparation stalled.
rows.caveat: A profit commitment is a promise by the sellers, not a result.
rows.curator_notes: Not the same entity as HK GEM 8236. Deal draft lists 57 sellers.

rows.name: Changjiang Computing
rows.origin: Founded 2020 by China Information and Communication Technology Group
rows.builds: Kunpeng and Ascend servers; won all four ARM packages of China Mobile's 2026-27 PC server tender
rows.revenue: Not disclosed separately (inside FiberHome's communications equipment line)
rows.funding: RMB 500m strategic capital increase, 2023-24 (total from one source)
rows.why: State-linked units inside listed telecom groups win the operators' ARM server tenders outright.
rows.caveat: Its output value is published; its revenue is not, and FiberHome says the two differ.

rows.name: Oxide Computer
rows.origin: Venture-backed start-up building a whole rack, boards to control plane
rows.builds: On-premises cloud racks on AMD EPYC for enterprise and government; not GPU racks
rows.revenue: Not disclosed; the company says it became profitable in 2026
rows.funding: US$44m Series A (2023), US$100m Series B (2025), US$200m Series C (Feb 2026), US$445m Series D (Oct 2026, led by Eclipse, with AMD Ventures)
rows.why: The only Western start-up re-architecting the whole rack; it competes for enterprise racks, not for the AI rack business of the ODMs.
rows.caveat: Round sizes are as announced; valuations circulating for the Series D were not verified.
rows.curator_notes: Series D: oxide.computer/blog/our-445m-series-d (2026-10-09) + DCD 2026-10-12. Series C: oxide.computer/blog/our-200m-series-c (2026-02-05); lead USIT per Axios only. Added after the 2026-11-09 verification pass found the card stale.

rows.name: Hyve Solutions
rows.origin: Rack-integration subsidiary of distributor TD SYNNEX
rows.status: Subsidiary of listed TD SYNNEX (not broken out)
rows.builds: Hyperscale servers and racks to customer design
rows.revenue: Not disclosed; gross billings up more than 50% year over year in the quarter to November 2025
rows.why: A distributor-owned integrator growing on hyperscaler racks shows the assembly layer is contestable outside the Taiwan ODMs.
rows.caveat: A growth rate of gross billings, not revenue, and no dollar figure.
rows.curator_notes: 'Top five hyperscalers' claim is a low-confidence media summary; not used.

rows.name: Bull
rows.status: Acquired by the French State (closed 2026-03-31, enterprise value up to EUR 404m)
rows.builds: HPC and AI systems for European public supercomputers
rows.why: Sovereign demand keeps a non-US, non-Asian system integrator alive, priced at a fraction of revenue.
rows.caveat: Revenue covers HPC, quantum and business computing, not AI servers alone.

rows.name: Aivres
rows.origin: Inspur's former US arm, renamed in 2023
rows.status: Reported to be owned by listed Inspur Information (IEIT)
rows.builds: NVIDIA GB200/GB300 NVL72 racks (company product pages)
rows.why: For a Chinese-owned US rack builder, ownership rather than capability is the binding constraint.
rows.caveat: Ownership is as reported by the press; Inspur's filings do not break Aivres out.
rows.curator_notes: Wholly-owned claim rests on a low-confidence secondary site; worded as 'reported'.

rows.name: Ingrasys and QCT
rows.origin: Rack and branded data-center arms of Foxconn Industrial Internet and Quanta
rows.status: Wholly owned inside listed parents (Ingrasys: 100% held by FII; QCT: Quanta)
rows.revenue: Inside the parents' figures; Ingrasys USA reported RMB 178.7bn of revenue in FII's 2026 interim report
rows.why: Listed for completeness: counting them beside their parents would double count.
rows.caveat: Not separate companies for any total on this page.
rows.curator_notes: FII 100% ownership of Ingrasys entities confirmed in FII H1 2026 report (A2 verification).
